sections.title: Compound Angle Formulas
sections.content: sin(A±B) = sinA cosB ± cosA sinB. cos(A±B) = cosA cosB ∓ sinA sinB (note the sign flip). tan(A±B) = (tanA ± tanB) / (1 ∓ tanA tanB).

sections.title: Multiple Angle Formulas (2θ and 3θ)
sections.content: sin2θ = 2sinθ cosθ = 2tanθ/(1+tan²θ). cos2θ = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ = (1-tan²θ)/(1+tan²θ). sin3θ = 3sinθ - 4sin³θ. cos3θ = 4cos³θ - 3cosθ.

sections.title: Transformation Formulas
sections.content: Converting products to sums: 2sinA cosB = sin(A+B) + sin(A-B). Converting sums to products: sinC + sinD = 2sin((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2).

sections.title: General Solutions of Trigonometric Equations
sections.content: If sinθ = sinα, then θ = nπ + (-1)^n α. If cosθ = cosα, then θ = 2nπ ± α. If tanθ = tanα, then θ = nπ + α. (Where 'n' is any integer).

sections.title: Form a cosθ + b sinθ
sections.content: An expression of the form a cosθ + b sinθ can be reduced to a single trig function: R cos(θ - α) or R sin(θ + α), where R = √(a² + b²) and tanα = b/a.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting the minus sign in cos(A+B).
2) Confusing the general solution of cos (2nπ ± α) with sin (nπ + (-1)^n α).
3) Dividing both sides of an equation by a variable trig function (like sinx), which loses valid solutions where sinx = 0.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 introduces the heavy algebraic lifting of trigonometry: expanding angles (A±B), doubling/tripling angles, transforming sums to products, and solving equations for general values of 'n'.

tricks.title: Max and Min Value of a cosθ + b sinθ
tricks.explanation: The maximum value is ALWAYS √(a² + b²) and the minimum value is ALWAYS -√(a² + b²).
tricks.example: Max value of 3sinθ + 4cosθ is √(3²+4²) = 5. Range is [-5, 5].

tricks.title: Values of 15° and 75°
tricks.explanation: Memorize these to save time instead of calculating sin(45-30) every time.

tricks.title: Cosine Product Series Trick
tricks.explanation: For a series where angles double: cosA * cos2A * cos4A * ... * cos(2^(n-1)A) = sin(2^n A) / (2^n * sinA).

tricks.title: tanA * tan(60-A) * tan(60+A)
tricks.explanation: This specific product simplifies directly to tan(3A). Works identically for sine and cosine (with a 1/4 multiplier for sin and cos).

tricks.title: Sum of Series in A.P.
tricks.explanation: If angles are in A.P. (α, α+β, α+2β...), the sum of sines is: [sin(nβ/2) / sin(β/2)] * sin(First + Last)/2.
tricks.example: sin(10) + sin(20) + sin(30)... applies this formula instantly without manual summation.

tricks.title: Graphical Intersections for Number of Solutions
tricks.explanation: When asked for the *number* of solutions between two functions (e.g., sinx = x/10), graph both and count intersection points rather than trying to solve algebraically.
tricks.example: sinx = x/10 intersects at the origin and repeatedly across peaks. Sketching it reveals 7 solutions.
